title: Why Sydney Sweeney’s ad has angered women athletes
description:
Sydney Sweeney has sparked controversy for a provocative ad campaign that appears to show her naked. It’s for the sports betting company Novig. In the advert, Sweeney is seen covering parts of her body with footballs, basketballs, golf clubs and other sports equipment and is heard repeating the word “sports.” But several women athletes — including Sophie Capewell, Amy Hunt, and Gracie Kramer — have criticised the campaign, saying it sexualises female athletes and views sport through the male gaze. Sweeney, who is best known for movies like ‘Anyone But You’ and ‘The Housemaid,’ hasn’t responded directly.

BBC Sport journalist Sarah Dawkins tells us more. We also hear from female athletes and content creators, including German rugby international Sofie Fella, Aofie Hernon, and Izza Khan.

summaryEn: This episode of BBC's What in the World examines the controversy surrounding a provocative ad for the sports betting app Novig, starring Hollywood actor Sydney Sweeney. In the commercial, Sweeney appears seemingly nude while strategically holding sports equipment. The campaign has sparked backlash from female athletes and creators, including Sophie Capewell and Gracie Kramer, who argue that it sexualizes women and reduces athletic achievements to the male gaze. While defenders point to body autonomy and marketing experts highlight how shock PR effectively boosts brand awareness, many female athletes emphasize that women's sports should be celebrated for skill and strength rather than appearance.
